It looks like your data might be corrupted (0-byte file at `file_path` I presume would result in this error). Do you still get the error if you remove `/home/jim/scikit_learn_data/lfw_home` first?

If this stops the error, you are welcome to submit a PR that makes the `check_fetch_lfw` function more robust.
Is this similar to the `newsgroup_download` error that we observed before?

I think there was something similar, yes, but don't really recall...

Were you executing this on MacOS? I'm facing the same problem here. Relevant version informations are:

```
$ python --version
Python 2.7.6

>>> import sklearn
>>> sklearn.__version__
'0.16.1'
>>> import numpy

'1.8.0rc1'

'0.13.0b1'
```

Have you tried removing the downloaded data set  file and rerunning the example?

Yes I've tried it. But it is still not working.
I've tried to read a file from the downloaded data set and even, it didn't work properly. I've tried as follows:

```
In [1]: from scipy import misc

In [2]: sharon = misc.imread("/Users/s52/scikit_learn_data/lfw_home/lfw_funneled/Ariel_Sharon/Ariel_Sharon_0001.jpg")

In [3]: sharon.shape
Out[3]: ()
```

I believe sharon.shape should output (512,512) or something similar.
Do you have PIL or Pillow installed?

Yes, I've installed PIL. After converting the file into png, it goes well.

```
In [18]: ArielSharon=misc.imread('/Users/s52/scikit_learn_data/lfw_home/lfw_funneled/Ariel_Sharon/Ariel_Sharon_0001.png')

In [19]: ArielSharon.shape
Out[19]: (250, 250, 3)
```

Yes, it was libjpeg problem and it was pretty tricky to install on MacOS X. But, I made it

```
In [1]: from scipy import misc

In [2]: ArielSharon=misc.imread('/Users/s52/scikit_learn_data/lfw_home/lfw_funneled/Ariel_Sharon/Ariel_Sharon_0001.jpg')

In [3]: ArielSharon.shape
Out[3]: (250, 250, 3)

```
how did you install numpy / scipy?

I used pip to install them, instead of Brew or MacPorts.  

Maybe, it would be fair enough to check if libjpeg exists in the system or not. For some reasons, I had png, but not jpeg.

Hum, are these wheels you installed? I am just wondering if this is not a symptom of a broken setup.
My train of thoughts is kinda "if you didn't link against libjpeg, you probably didn't link against a decent blas".
but yeah, we should check if the jpeg reading worked and give an appropriate error message.

body:
FYI, I have a perfectly good version of libjpeg installed but I was still getting this message.  

In my case I was able to fix it by upgrading to the latest version of Pillow.  this ensures that `imread` is loaded from Pillow and not from scipy.
scipy doesn't have an imread, it is always in pillow... but your previous pillow wasn't compiled with libjpeg support.
